key_insight: Blackjack uses just two cfDNA fragmentation-similarity features to distinguish cancer from healthy samples, including early-stage cancers.
clinical_relevance: This blood-based detection approach could support multi-cancer screening research; it is not a drug discovery method or an established clinical screening test.
method: Encode DNA sequence context around cfDNA fragmentation sites in a position probability matrix.
Measure similarity to matrices from known healthy and cancer cohorts.
Use the two similarity features in logistic regression to classify samples.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation on two external whole-genome sequencing datasets yielded a minimum AUC of 0.993 and sensitivity of 91.8% at 98% specificity; stage I sensitivity was 89.8%.
watch_item: Cross-validation performance does not establish real-world screening benefit; prospective validation in intended screening populations is needed.
paper_title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
